---
title: "Assignment, feature, and effect API"
subtitle: "Configuration, probability laws, metadata, and validation"
---

```{python}
import inspect

import numpy as np
import pypanelsim as pps


def show_signature(object_):
    print(f"{object_.__name__}{inspect.signature(object_)}")
```

## `GaussianUnitFeatures`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.GaussianUnitFeatures)
```

Draws independent standard-normal `observables` and `unobservables` matrices.

| Parameter | Default | Contract |
|---|---:|---|
| `n_observables` | `2` | Nonnegative feature count |
| `n_unobservables` | `2` | Nonnegative latent-feature count |

Metadata includes `kind="gaussian_unit_features"`, `observable_names`, and
`unobservable_names`. A zero count returns an `(n_units, 0)` matrix without
consuming draws for that block.

## `GaussianTimeFeatures`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.GaussianTimeFeatures)
```

Draws an `(n_periods, n_features)` matrix of independent standard-normal time
features. `n_features` defaults to one and must be nonnegative. Metadata records
`kind="gaussian_time_features"` and names `v1`, `v2`, and so on. Supply a custom
`TimeFeatureModel` when $V_t$ should be a trend, cycle, shock process, or
calendar covariate.

## `SingleCohortAssignment`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.SingleCohortAssignment)
```

Creates one deterministic absorbing cohort.

| Parameter | Default | Contract |
|---|---:|---|
| `n_treated` | `40` | Between one and `n_units` |
| `adoption_period` | `40` | Zero-based valid period |
| `treated_units` | `None` | Optional unique tuple of exactly `n_treated` valid positions |

When positions are omitted, the last `n_treated` rows are treated. The model
does not consume random draws. Metadata records the positions and adoption
period.

## `RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.RandomizedSingleCohortAssignment)
```

Samples a fixed number of units without replacement, then treats them from a
common adoption period onward.

| Parameter | Contract |
|---|---|
| `n_treated` | Positive and no larger than the eligible count |
| `adoption_period` | Zero-based valid period |
| `eligible_units` | Optional unique valid positions; default is every unit |

For eligible set $E$, each eligible unit has marginal probability
$n_{treated}/|E|$. Metadata contains `treated_units`, `eligible_units`,
`adoption_period`, and the unit-aligned `propensity_scores` vector.

## `RandomizedStaggeredAdoption`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.RandomizedStaggeredAdoption)
```

Randomly partitions eligible units into exact fixed-size absorbing adoption
cohorts. `adoption_periods` and `cohort_sizes` are paired positionally; sampled
cohorts are disjoint, and unsampled units remain untreated. Metadata contains
cohort unit positions, realized categories and adoption times, and the marginal
generalized propensity score over every cohort plus never treated. Ineligible
units have probability one on the never-treated category.

## `BinaryLogitAssignment`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.BinaryLogitAssignment)
```

Draws independent eventual-treatment indicators using

$$
P(D_i=1\mid X_i,U_i)=
\Lambda(\alpha+X_i^\top\beta+U_i^\top\gamma).
$$

| Parameter | Default | Contract |
|---|---:|---|
| `adoption_period` | Required | Zero-based valid period |
| `intercept` | `0.0` | Finite scalar |
| `observable_coefficients` | `()` | One finite coefficient per observed feature |
| `unobservable_coefficients` | `()` | One finite coefficient per latent feature |

The coefficient counts must exactly match `AssignmentContext`. Unlike fixed-size
randomization, the treated count is random and all-treated or all-control draws
are possible in small/extreme designs. Metadata contains the linear predictor,
sigmoid probabilities, realized treated units, coefficient vectors, and adoption
period.

## `StaggeredAdoption`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.StaggeredAdoption)
```

Accepts a mapping `{unit_position: adoption_period}` and constructs absorbing
treatment. Units absent from the mapping are never treated. The mapping is
copied at construction. Invalid unit or time positions raise `ValueError`.

## `GeneralizedPropensityAssignment`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.GeneralizedPropensityAssignment)
```

Maps each unit to one adoption cohort or never treated. For $G$ supplied
adoption periods, coefficient rows correspond to those periods in caller order.
Never treated is category `G` with normalized logit zero.

| Parameter | Shape | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `adoption_periods` | `(G,)` | Nonempty, unique, valid zero-based periods |
| `intercepts` | `(G,)` | Finite; omitted means zeros |
| `observable_coefficients` | `(G,K_x)` | Finite; omitted means zeros |
| `unobservable_coefficients` | `(G,K_u)` | Finite; omitted means zeros |

Probabilities use a stable row-wise softmax. One uniform draw maps each unit to a
category; treatment is one from the realized adoption period onward.

Metadata keys:

| Key | Shape or value |
|---|---|
| `generalized_propensity_scores` | `(N,G+1)`; rows sum to one |
| `cohort_linear_predictors` | `(N,G)` |
| `assigned_categories` | `(N,)`; `G` denotes never treated |
| `adoption_times` | `(N,)`; never treated uses `n_periods` |
| `adoption_periods` | `(G,)` |
| `never_treated_category` | Integer `G` |
| coefficient/intercept keys | Normalized NumPy arrays used in the draw |

## `ConstantEffect`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.ConstantEffect)
```

Returns `value * context.treatment`. `value` defaults to `1.0` and must be
finite. Metadata records `kind="constant"` and the value.

## `LinearRampEffect`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.LinearRampEffect)
```

For adoption time $G_i$, returns

$$
\tau_{it}=s\max(t-G_i+1,0)W_{it}.
$$

`slope` defaults to `0.2` and must be finite. The effect supports staggered
absorbing adoption because event time is unit specific. Nonabsorbing treatment
raises through `context.adoption_times`.

## `CallableEffect`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.CallableEffect)
```

Adapts a deterministic effect law to `EffectModel`. Its callable receives
`SimulationContext`, including `observables`, `unobservables`, and
`time_features`. It can therefore implement
$\tau_{it}=f(X_i,U_i,V_t)$. Accepted results are:

| Returned shape | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| scalar | Common across units and time |
| `(N,)` or `(N,1)` | Unit effect, broadcast over time |
| `(T,)` or `(1,T)` | Time effect, broadcast over units |
| `(N,T)` | Complete unit-by-time effect surface |

The realized matrix is

$$
\tau_{it}^{\mathrm{realized}}=f(X_i,U_i,V_t)W_{it}.
$$

The normalized `(N,T)` law is recorded under `effect_surface`. Pure unit and
time laws additionally record `unit_effects` or `time_effects`. Metadata also
identifies the normalization type. For a square panel, a one-dimensional vector
retains the legacy unit interpretation; return `(1,T)` for an unambiguous time
law. A malformed or nonfinite result raises `ValueError`.

```{python}
effect = pps.CallableEffect(
    lambda x: (
        1.0 + 0.5 * x.observables[:, 0] + x.unobservables[:, 0]
    )[:, None] * (1.0 + 0.25 * x.time_features[:, 0])[None, :],
    name="unit_time_heterogeneity",
)
```

For the common case, pass the lambda directly to `PanelSimulator` and it will
be wrapped automatically. `CallableUnitEffect` remains a backward-compatible
class name and accepts the same result shapes.

## `CohortEventTimeEffect`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.CohortEventTimeEffect)
```

Accepts `{adoption_period: post_adoption_vector}` and applies each vector by
unit-specific event time. Treatment must be absorbing. Every realized cohort
must have a supplied profile long enough to cover its treated cells. This is a
generic effect component used by the F-test paper catalog and is equally usable
in custom staggered-adoption designs.

## `CallableOutcomeModel`

```{python}
show_signature(pps.CallableOutcomeModel)
```

Adapts a plain callable `(SimulationContext, Generator) -> matrix | ComponentDraw`
to `OutcomeModel`. Matrix results are wrapped in `ComponentDraw` with
`kind=name`; a returned `ComponentDraw` is preserved. Final shape and finiteness
remain the simulator's responsibility.
